quote: The "SEQUENCE" property is used by the "Organizer" to indicate revisions to the calendar component.
test: Local PARTSTAT edit on an invitation where we are only an attendee (SEQUENCE:3) must emit SEQUENCE:3 unchanged.

quote: When the "Organizer" makes changes to one of the following properties, the sequence number MUST be incremented:
test: update_event on an event whose ORGANIZER is our address changes DTSTART (list: DTSTART, DTEND, DURATION, DUE, RRULE, RDATE, EXDATE, STATUS): SEQUENCE goes from n to n+1, absent SEQUENCE counts as 0 and becomes 1.

quote: In addition, changes made by the "Organizer" to other properties MAY also require the sequence number to be incremented.
test: Organizer edit that only changes SUMMARY: per POLICY:sequence-organizer-bump SEQUENCE stays unchanged.

quote: The "SEQUENCE" property value MUST NOT be incremented when using "REPLY", "REFRESH", "COUNTER", "DECLINECOUNTER", or when sending a delegation "REQUEST".
test: respond_to_event ACCEPTED on an event with SEQUENCE:2 leaves SEQUENCE:2 byte-identical.

quote: The "SEQUENCE" property value MUST be incremented each time the "Organizer" uses the "ADD" or "CANCEL" methods.
test: No ADD/CANCEL message is emitted; end_event_series as organizer changes RRULE, so SEQUENCE+1 follows from RFC5546:2.1.4:increment-on-trigger-properties.
reason: We do not send iTIP messages (ADD, CANCEL); the stored-object consequence is covered by the RRULE trigger row.

quote: To reference an instance of a recurring component, the primary key is composed of the "UID" and the "RECURRENCE-ID" properties.
test: File with master (UID u) and override (UID u, RECURRENCE-ID 20261121T100000Z): editing the instance 2026-11-21 changes the override only, never the master.

quote: the component with the highest numeric value for the "SEQUENCE" property obsoletes all other revisions of the component with lower values.
test: Master SEQUENCE:2 and override SEQUENCE:1 stay as they are after an unrelated edit; no renumbering of either component.

quote: In situations where the "UID", "RECURRENCE-ID", and "SEQUENCE" property values match, the "DTSTAMP" property is used as the tie-breaker. The component with the latest "DTSTAMP" overrides all others.
test: Local PARTSTAT edit of a file whose DTSTAMP is 20261114T100000Z with clock 20261114T101500Z writes DTSTAMP:20261114T101500Z (strictly later than before, never earlier).

quote: Hence, CUAs will need to persist the following component properties in order to correctly process iTIP messages: "UID", "RECURRENCE-ID", "SEQUENCE", and "DTSTAMP".
test: Any rewrite keeps UID, RECURRENCE-ID (with its TZID/VALUE/RANGE parameters), SEQUENCE:5 and a DTSTAMP on every VEVENT; SEQUENCE:5 is never dropped.

quote: Value MUST be 2.0.
test: new_event output contains exactly one VERSION:2.0 and one PRODID line inside VCALENDAR.

quote: The "Organizer" MUST be present in a published iCalendar component.
test: Event with ORGANIZER and no ATTENDEE parses and can be edited without adding an ATTENDEE; see POLICY:organizer-without-attendee-valid.
reason: Describes PUBLISH messages, which we never send; it only shows that ORGANIZER without ATTENDEE is a legal shape.

quote: "Attendees" MUST NOT be present.
test: update_event on an ORGANIZER-only event never introduces an ATTENDEE line.
reason: PUBLISH-message rule; we send no iTIP. The stored-object behaviour is POLICY:organizer-without-attendee-valid.

quote: The new "Organizer" should then send out a new "REQUEST" with a modified version of the "VEVENT" in which the "SEQUENCE" number has been incremented and the "ORGANIZER" property has been changed to the new "Organizer".
test: update_event asking to change ORGANIZER returns an error and writes nothing; see POLICY:refuse-organizer-change.
reason: Requires sending a REQUEST to attendees, which we cannot do; handled by policy refusal.

quote: The recipient SHOULD respond with a "REPLY" method indicating their current status with respect to the "REQUEST".
test: respond_to_event only edits the stored file; no REPLY message is created (documented in the tool description).
reason: REPLY emission is out of scope: we do not send iTIP.

quote: The optional properties listed in the table below (those listed as "0+" or "0 or 1") MUST NOT be changed from those of the original request.
test: A generated REPLY would carry SUMMARY/DTSTART unchanged; here the equivalent is POLICY:respond-local-partstat-only.
reason: REPLY emission is out of scope; the stored-edit equivalent is the policy row.

quote: MUST be the address of the Attendee replying.
test: REPLY table: ATTENDEE presence 1, address of the replier (table cell is wrapped by pipe characters, so the quote is the cell text). A stored edit changes only the ATTENDEE line matching our address.
reason: REPLY emission is out of scope; the stored-edit equivalent is POLICY:respond-local-partstat-only.

quote: Only if referring to an instance of a recurring calendar component. Otherwise, it MUST NOT be present.
test: REPLY table row RECURRENCE-ID (0 or 1): a whole-series response carries no RECURRENCE-ID, an instance response carries it; the stored equivalent is POLICY:respond-instance-override.
reason: REPLY emission is out of scope; the quote text is wrapped by table pipes in the source.

quote: If non-zero, MUST be the sequence number of the original REQUEST.
test: REPLY SEQUENCE equals the stored SEQUENCE when non-zero; in the stored-edit flow SEQUENCE is simply unchanged.
reason: REPLY emission is out of scope.

quote: An "Attendee" MAY include a message to the "Organizer" using the "COMMENT" property.
test: respond_to_event does not add a COMMENT property to the stored event.
reason: A COMMENT only exists to reach the organizer inside a REPLY we do not send.

quote: In addition, the "REPLY" method may be received from an unknown CU (a "Party Crasher").
test: Organizer-side behaviour only; for us see POLICY:reject-respond-when-not-attendee.
reason: Describes how an organizer treats unknown repliers; we are the replier, not the organizer.

quote: To cancel the complete range of a recurring event, the "UID" property value for the event MUST be specified and a "RECURRENCE-ID" MUST NOT be specified in the "CANCEL" method.
test: No CANCEL is emitted; deleting a whole series is a file deletion of the UID's file, never a RECURRENCE-ID stub.
reason: CANCEL emission is out of scope: we do not send iTIP.

quote: The "RECURRENCE-ID" property for an instance in the sequence MUST be specified with the "RANGE" property parameter value of "THISANDFUTURE" to indicate cancellation of the specified "VEVENT" calendar component and all instances after.
test: end_event_series does not write RANGE=THISANDFUTURE; it truncates the master RRULE (see POLICY:end-series-truncate-rrule).
reason: CANCEL emission is out of scope; we truncate the stored RRULE instead.

quote: When a "VEVENT" is cancelled, the "SEQUENCE" property value MUST be incremented as described in Section 2.1.4.
test: end_event_series as organizer raises SEQUENCE by one through the RRULE trigger rule; as non-organizer it leaves SEQUENCE unchanged.
reason: Applies to CANCEL messages; the stored-edit effect is covered by RFC5546:2.1.4:increment-on-trigger-properties.

quote: Hence, implementations that choose to maintain per-instance properties (such as "ATTENDEE" property "PARTSTAT" parameter) may do so.
test: Declining one instance of a weekly series produces a VEVENT override (UID u, RECURRENCE-ID of that instance) with PARTSTAT=DECLINED while the master keeps its PARTSTAT.

quote: However, the protocol does not require per-instance recognition unless the instance itself must be renegotiated.
test: Responding to the whole series changes the master's ATTENDEE PARTSTAT only and leaves existing overrides untouched.

quote: An instance of a recurring event is assigned a unique identification, "RECURRENCE-ID" property, when that instance is renegotiated.
test: A new override created for instance 2026-11-21T10:00 uses RECURRENCE-ID equal to the original DTSTART of that instance.

quote: Failing (2), the CUA MAY ignore or accept the request as the "Calendar User" wishes.
test: respond_to_event for an address not in any ATTENDEE (and no group/CUTYPE match) returns an error and leaves the file untouched.

quote: A client SHOULD save "iana-token's" and MAY use them in replies.
test: A rewrite keeps unknown IANA properties, e.g. CONFERENCE and IMAGE, byte-for-byte.

quote: A client MAY save "x-name's" and MAY use them in replies.
test: X-WR-CALNAME at VCALENDAR level and X-APPLE-* properties on the VEVENT survive an edit unchanged.

quote: This property MUST be specified in an iCalendar object that specifies a group-scheduled calendar entity.
test: An event that has ATTENDEE lines is a group-scheduled entity and therefore must also have ORGANIZER; see RFC5545:3.8.4.3:organizer-in-group-scheduled.

quote: This property MUST be specified in an iCalendar object that specifies a group-scheduled calendar entity.
test: Input with ATTENDEE;PARTSTAT=NEEDS-ACTION:mailto:me@x and no ORGANIZER: respond_to_event returns an error, file unchanged (POLICY:respond-requires-organizer).

quote: This property MUST NOT be specified in an iCalendar object that specifies only a time zone definition or that defines calendar components that are not group-scheduled components, but are components only on a single user's calendar.
test: new_event without attendees writes no ORGANIZER line, so a private single-user event is not turned into a scheduling object.

quote: The values MUST match one of the values allowed for the given calendar component.
test: respond_to_event accepts ACCEPTED, DECLINED, TENTATIVE (VEVENT also allows NEEDS-ACTION and DELEGATED) and rejects COMPLETED or MAYBE without writing.

quote: If not specified on a property that allows this parameter, the default value is NEEDS-ACTION.
test: ATTENDEE:mailto:me@x without PARTSTAT reads as NEEDS-ACTION; after respond ACCEPTED the line carries exactly one PARTSTAT=ACCEPTED parameter.

quote: Applications MUST treat x-name and iana-token values they don't recognize the same way as they would the NEEDS-ACTION value.
test: ATTENDEE;PARTSTAT=X-FOO:mailto:me@x is read as NEEDS-ACTION in listings, but the raw token is kept if the line is not edited.

quote: This property MUST have the same value type as the "DTSTART" property contained within the recurring component.
test: Master DTSTART;VALUE=DATE:20261120 gives an override RECURRENCE-ID;VALUE=DATE:20261127, not a date-time.

quote: Furthermore, this property MUST be specified as a date with local time if and only if the "DTSTART" property contained within the recurring component is specified as a date with local time.
test: Floating master DTSTART:20261120T100000 gives RECURRENCE-ID:20261127T100000 (no Z, no TZID); a UTC master gives a Z value.

quote: Subsequent instances are determined by their "RECURRENCE-ID" value and not their current scheduled start time.
test: An instance rescheduled by an override keeps matching its original RECURRENCE-ID slot, so it is neither duplicated nor dropped by a THISANDFUTURE range.
reason: Goes with deferred RANGE=THISANDFUTURE expansion.

quote: In such cases, the calendar application could simply truncate the unbounded recurring calendar component (i.e., with the "COUNT" or "UNTIL" rule parts)
test: end_event_series on RRULE:FREQ=WEEKLY writes RRULE:FREQ=WEEKLY;UNTIL=<last instance>, which is the RFC-sanctioned way to end a series.

quote: The value of the UNTIL rule part MUST have the same value type as the "DTSTART" property.
test: DTSTART;VALUE=DATE:20261120 yields UNTIL=20261204 (a DATE, no time part).

quote: Furthermore, if the "DTSTART" property is specified as a date with local time, then the UNTIL rule part MUST also be specified as a date with local time.
test: Floating DTSTART:20261120T100000 yields UNTIL=20261204T100000 without Z (corrects the earlier matrix, which omitted the floating case).

quote: If the "DTSTART" property is specified as a date with UTC time or a date with local time and time zone reference, then the UNTIL rule part MUST be specified as a date with UTC time.
test: DTSTART;TZID=Europe/Berlin:20261120T100000 with last instance 2026-12-04 10:00 local gives UNTIL=20261204T090000Z (converted to UTC, winter offset +01:00).

quote: If specified as a DATE-TIME value, then it MUST be specified in a UTC time format.
test: This sentence conflicts with the floating-DTSTART rule above (ambiguity in the RFC); we follow the specific floating rule for floating DTSTART and accept both forms when parsing.

quote: The UNTIL or COUNT rule parts are OPTIONAL, but they MUST NOT occur in the same 'recur'.
test: RRULE:FREQ=DAILY;COUNT=10 ended by end_event_series becomes FREQ=DAILY;UNTIL=... with COUNT removed (the source ABNF comment lines are interleaved with semicolons, so the quote is normalised).
Series with RDATE:20270105T100000Z ended at 2026-12-05: the RDATE after the cutoff is removed too, because UNTIL does not bound RDATE instances.

quote: A BACKSLASH character in a "TEXT" property value MUST be escaped with another BACKSLASH character.
test: SUMMARY value a\b is written SUMMARY:a\\b and read back as a\b.

quote: A COMMA character in a "TEXT" property value MUST be escaped with a BACKSLASH character.
test: LOCATION value Room 1, Berlin is written LOCATION:Room 1\, Berlin.

quote: A SEMICOLON character in a "TEXT" property value MUST be escaped with a BACKSLASH character.
test: SUMMARY value a;b is written SUMMARY:a\;b.

quote: An intentional formatted text line break MUST only be included in a "TEXT" property value by representing the line break with the character sequence of BACKSLASH, followed by a LATIN SMALL LETTER N or a LATIN CAPITAL LETTER N, that is "\n" or "\N".
test: DESCRIPTION with two lines is written DESCRIPTION:line1\nline2 on one logical line; both \n and \N decode to a newline.

quote: Property parameter values that contain the COLON, SEMICOLON, or COMMA character separators MUST be specified as quoted-string text values.
test: CN value Smith, Jane is written ATTENDEE;CN="Smith, Jane":mailto:... (quoted, no backslash).

quote: Property parameter values MUST NOT contain the DQUOTE character.
test: A CN containing a double quote is never written raw; it is encoded per RFC 6868 (^') or the value is rejected.

quote: Content lines are delimited by a line break, which is a CRLF sequence (CR character followed by LF character).
test: Written files contain only CRLF line endings (no bare LF); parsing also accepts a file that has bare LF.

quote: Lines of text SHOULD NOT be longer than 75 octets, excluding the line break.
test: A 200-character DESCRIPTION is written as lines of at most 75 octets (continuations start with one space); corrected from the earlier matrix, which called folding a plain SHOULD.

quote: It is possible for very simple implementations to generate improperly folded lines in the middle of a UTF-8 multi-octet sequence.
test: Folding a SUMMARY of 30 two-byte characters never splits a character between two lines; parsing a file that was split mid-sequence restores the original bytes.

quote: Applications that support importing iCalendar objects SHOULD support all of the component types defined in this document, and SHOULD NOT silently drop any components as that can lead to user data loss.
test: A file with VEVENT plus an unknown X-COMP or VALARM keeps every component after an edit; if a component cannot be preserved the edit is refused instead.

quote: Applications MUST ignore x-param and iana-param values they don't recognize.
test: ATTENDEE;X-NUM-GUESTS=2;PARTSTAT=ACCEPTED:mailto:me@x parses fine; editing PARTSTAT keeps X-NUM-GUESTS=2.

quote: The following is REQUIRED if the component appears in an iCalendar object that doesn't specify the "METHOD" property
test: A stored VEVENT has DTSTART; since stored files carry no METHOD, a VEVENT without DTSTART is reported as invalid by the reader (the source lines are interleaved with ABNF comment semicolons).

quote: 'dtend' and 'duration' MUST NOT occur in the same 'eventprop'.
test: Changing an event with DURATION:PT1H to a new end replaces DURATION with DTEND (never both).

quote: If such a "VEVENT" has a "DTEND" property, it MUST be specified as a DATE value also.
test: All-day event DTSTART;VALUE=DATE:20261120 gets DTEND;VALUE=DATE:20261121 when shifted, never a date-time.

quote: This property MUST be included in the "VEVENT", "VTODO", "VJOURNAL", or "VFREEBUSY" calendar components.
test: Editing an event that has no DTSTAMP adds one; every VEVENT in the output has exactly one DTSTAMP.

quote: In the case of an iCalendar object that doesn't specify a "METHOD" property, this property is equivalent to the "LAST-MODIFIED" property.
test: With no METHOD in the file, a local edit sets DTSTAMP and LAST-MODIFIED to the same instant (confirms the earlier note: refresh both on a local change; no RFC states it as a MUST for edits).

quote: When a calendar component is created, its sequence number is 0.
test: new_event writes SEQUENCE:0 or omits SEQUENCE (RFC 5546 allows both when 0); never SEQUENCE:1.

quote: It is monotonically incremented by the "Organizer's" CUA each time the "Organizer" makes a significant revision to the calendar component.
test: Confirms that SEQUENCE is changed by the organizer's client only: attendee-side edit leaves SEQUENCE alone, organizer-side significant edit adds exactly 1 (never decreases).

quote: Recurrence instances of a recurring component MAY have different sequence numbers.
test: Master SEQUENCE:2 with override SEQUENCE:0 stays valid; editing the master does not rewrite the override's SEQUENCE.

quote: This specification defines the ^ character (U+005E -- Circumflex Accent) as an escape character in parameter values whose value type is defined using the "param-value" syntax element
test: ATTENDEE;CN="Smith^n, J":mailto:x and ATTENDEE;CN=Smith^nJ:mailto:x both decode ^n to a line break (quoted and unquoted values).

quote: formatted text line breaks are encoded into ^n (U+005E, U+006E)
test: A generated CN value with an embedded line feed is written with ^n and no raw newline in the content line.

quote: the ^ character (U+005E) is encoded into ^^ (U+005E, U+005E)
test: CN value a^b is written CN=a^^b.

quote: the " character (U+0022) is encoded into ^' (U+005E, U+0027)
test: CN value George Herman "Babe" Ruth is written ATTENDEE;CN=George Herman ^'Babe^' Ruth:mailto:babe@example.com (RFC 6868 section 3.1 example).

quote: the character sequence ^n (U+005E, U+006E) is decoded into an appropriate formatted line break according to the type of system being used
test: CN=Pittsburgh Pirates^n115 Federal St decodes to two lines.

quote: the character sequence ^^ (U+005E, U+005E) is decoded into the ^ character (U+005E)
test: CN=a^^b decodes to a^b.

quote: the character sequence ^' (U+005E, U+0027) is decoded into the " character (U+0022)
test: CN=George Herman ^'Babe^' Ruth decodes to George Herman "Babe" Ruth.

quote: if a ^ (U+005E) character is followed by any character other than the ones above, parsers MUST leave both the ^ and the following character in place
test: CN=a^xb decodes to a^xb; if that ATTENDEE line is rewritten without changing CN, the raw text a^xb is kept (re-encoding to a^^xb would corrupt the file).

quote: The \-escaping mechanism used for property text values is not defined for use with parameter values and cannot be easily used in a backwards-compatible manner.
test: A parameter value containing a comma is quoted (CN="a,b"), never written as CN=a\,b; a property TEXT value still uses backslash escapes.

quote: Calendar object resources contained in calendar collections MUST NOT contain more than one type of calendar component (e.g., VEVENT, VTODO, VJOURNAL, VFREEBUSY, etc.) with the exception of VTIMEZONE components,
test: A file holding one VEVENT and one VTODO is not rewritten by the event tools (error, file untouched); new_event files hold VEVENT and VTIMEZONE only.

quote: VTIMEZONE components, which MUST be specified for each unique TZID parameter value specified in the iCalendar object.
test: Moving an event to DTSTART;TZID=America/New_York adds a VTIMEZONE with TZID:America/New_York (once); a TZID used by DTSTART, DTEND, EXDATE and RECURRENCE-ID yields exactly one VTIMEZONE; a still-referenced VTIMEZONE is never dropped.

quote: Calendar object resources contained in calendar collections MUST NOT specify the iCalendar METHOD property.
test: Input with METHOD:REQUEST (e.g. saved from an e-mail invitation): the rewritten file has no METHOD line (POLICY:strip-method-on-write); stored files written by new_event never contain one.

quote: The UID property value of the calendar components contained in a calendar object resource MUST be unique in the scope of the calendar collection in which they are stored.
test: new_event with a UID already present in another file of the calendar directory fails and writes nothing.

quote: Calendar components in a calendar collection that have different UID property values MUST be stored in separate calendar object resources.
test: A file containing VEVENTs with UIDs a and b is flagged as invalid; the event tools refuse to edit it instead of guessing.

quote: Calendar components with the same UID property value, in a given calendar collection, MUST be contained in the same calendar object resource.
test: Creating an override for instance X of series u appends the VEVENT to the existing file of u; no second file with UID u is created.

quote: It is possible for a calendar object resource to just contain components that represent "overridden" instances (ones that modify the behavior of a regular instance, and thus include a RECURRENCE-ID property) without also including the "master" recurring component
test: File with only a RECURRENCE-ID VEVENT (no master) is listed as a single event at its own time and can be edited without a master being required.

quote: This specification models a recurring calendar component and its recurrence exceptions as a single resource.
test: Master and all RECURRENCE-ID overrides of one series live in exactly one .ics file.

quote: The URL for each calendar object resource is entirely arbitrary and does not need to bear a specific relationship to the calendar object resource's iCalendar properties or other metadata.
test: Corrects the earlier matrix (section 4.2 has no naming rule): an existing file named foo.ics holding UID u is found by UID, not by file name.

quote: the URL of calendar object resources containing (an arbitrary set of) calendaring and scheduling information may be suffixed by ".ics"
test: new_event names the file <sanitised-uid>.ics.

quote: the client SHOULD use the HTTP request header "If-None-Match: *" on the PUT request.
test: new_event creates the file exclusively (fails if the name exists, e.g. open with wx or link()) so a concurrent or repeated call cannot overwrite an existing event.

quote: MUST NOT specify an iCalendar UID property value already in use in the targeted calendar collection or overwrite an existing calendar object resource with one that has a different UID property value.
test: update_event rewriting file f.ics never changes the UID inside it; the output UID equals the input UID on every component.

quote: this specification recommends that all properties not defined in [RFC5545] always include a "VALUE" parameter if the type is other than "TEXT".
test: A generated CONFERENCE line is CONFERENCE;VALUE=URI:https://meet.example/x; IMAGE uses VALUE=URI or VALUE=BINARY.
reason: The server writes none of the properties RFC 7986 adds (COLOR, IMAGE, CONFERENCE, NAME, ...); existing ones are preserved verbatim, VALUE parameters included.

quote: This property specifies the name of the calendar.
test: A VCALENDAR-level NAME (and the vendor X-WR-CALNAME, which RFC 7986 does not mention) is preserved unchanged on an event edit and not used as event data.

quote: However, each property MUST represent the name of the calendar in a different language.
test: Two NAME lines with different LANGUAGE parameters are both kept; we never write two NAME lines of one language.

quote: "UID" values MUST NOT include any data that might identify a user, host, domain, or any other security- or privacy-sensitive information.
test: new_event UID matches a random UUID and contains neither the user's e-mail, the host name nor any domain.

quote: It is RECOMMENDED that calendar user agents now generate "UID" values that are hex-encoded random Universally Unique Identifier (UUID) values as defined in Sections 4.4 and 4.5 of [RFC4122].
test: new_event UID matches ^[0-9a-f]{8}-[0-9a-f]{4}-4[0-9a-f]{3}-[89ab][0-9a-f]{3}-[0-9a-f]{12}$ (random from an injected source, not read inside the function).
reason: The UID is a random UUID v4 (randomUUID at the process edge) followed by the fixed suffix @mcp-khal, which split-off series also use; the value is therefore not a bare UUID. Dropping the suffix is a separate decision.

quote: they MUST have a length less than 255 octets and MUST conform to the "iana-token" ABNF syntax defined in Section 3.1 of [RFC5545].
test: If a caller-supplied UID is accepted it must be under 255 octets and consist of letters, digits and hyphens only; a UID with / or .. is rejected (also protects the file name).

quote: This property can be specified once in an iCalendar object or in "VEVENT", "VTODO", or "VJOURNAL" calendar components.
test: Setting a colour on an event that already has COLOR replaces that line; the VEVENT never ends up with two COLOR lines.
reason: No tool sets a colour: the server never writes COLOR and leaves an existing COLOR line untouched.

quote: The value is a case-insensitive color name taken from the CSS3 set of names, defined in Section 4.3 of [W3C.REC-css3-color-20110607].
test: COLOR:Turquoise is accepted; a generated COLOR value is a CSS3 name (COLOR:turquoise), not #40e0d0; a vdir color file is a different thing (VDIR:color-format).
reason: The server never generates COLOR and does not interpret colour names, so there is no value to validate; an existing COLOR is preserved verbatim.

quote: This property specifies a color that clients MAY use when presenting the relevant data to a user.
test: An event with an unknown colour name is still listed and editable; the colour is ignored for display, not rejected.

quote: The value MUST be data with a media type of "image" or refer to such data.
test: IMAGE;VALUE=BINARY;ENCODING=BASE64;FMTTYPE=image/png:<folded base64> survives a rewrite byte-for-byte (including its fold points after re-unfolding and re-folding).

quote: The following is OPTIONAL for a URI value, RECOMMENDED for a BINARY value, and MUST NOT occur more than once.
test: ABNF allows VALUE=URI, or ENCODING=BASE64 together with VALUE=BINARY; an IMAGE written by us never has ENCODING without VALUE=BINARY (quote is the FMTTYPE ABNF comment, lines interleaved with semicolons).
reason: We do not create IMAGE properties; the rule matters only if image support is added.

quote: The format type parameter can be specified on this property and is RECOMMENDED for inline binary-encoded content information.
test: If we ever write inline IMAGE we include FMTTYPE; existing FMTTYPE is preserved.
reason: We do not create IMAGE properties; existing ones are preserved only.

quote: In the absence of this parameter, the default value "BADGE" MUST be used.
test: IMAGE without DISPLAY reads as DISPLAY=BADGE; the parameter is not added when the line is rewritten.
reason: We do not render images; only preservation matters.

quote: This property can be specified multiple times in a "VEVENT" or "VTODO" calendar component.
test: Two CONFERENCE lines on one VEVENT are both preserved in order.

quote: The following is REQUIRED, but MUST NOT occur more than once.
test: CONFERENCE;VALUE=URI;FEATURE=AUDIO,VIDEO;LABEL=Join:https://chat.example/x is preserved exactly; a generated CONFERENCE always has VALUE=URI (quote is the ABNF comment above the VALUE=URI alternative; lines interleaved with semicolons).

quote: In iTIP messages [iTIP], only the "Organizer" is authorized to modify or cancel calendar entries she organizes.
test: update_event changing DTSTART on an event whose ORGANIZER is someone else: the policy decides (warn in the tool result); the RFC constrains messages, not local files.
reason: Authorization rule for iMIP messages; we process no messages. See POLICY:non-organizer-edit-is-local.

quote: Furthermore, only the respondent has the authorization to indicate their status to the "Organizer".
test: respond_to_event changes only the PARTSTAT of the ATTENDEE that matches our own address, never another attendee's.

quote: The calendar address specified within the "ORGANIZER" and "ATTENDEE" properties in an iCalendar object sent using iMIP MUST be a proper "mailto:" [MAILTO] URI specification
test: Any ATTENDEE or ORGANIZER we generate has the form mailto:<address>; matching our own address ignores the case of the mailto: scheme.

quote: The value MUST be the same (ignoring case) as the value of the "METHOD" property within the iCalendar object.
test: Not testable here: we create no MIME messages. RFC 6047 says nothing about stored objects (confirmed), so METHOD handling in stores rests on RFC 4791 and POLICY:strip-method-on-write.
reason: iMIP transport rule; we never build iMIP messages.

quote: The file *must* contain exactly one event, task or contact.
test: new_event writes one file holding exactly one UID (one VEVENT plus VTIMEZONEs).

quote: Recurrence exceptions are the exception, since they can need several event components in one file.
test: A series with two overrides is one file with three VEVENTs sharing one UID (page text paraphrased by the fetch tool, not copied verbatim).

quote: An item *should* contain a `UID` property as described by the vCard and iCalendar standards.
test: new_event always writes a UID; a file without UID is listed but the edit tools report it cannot be addressed by UID.

quote: If it contains more than one `UID` property, the values of those *must* not differ.
test: A file with VEVENTs of UID a and UID b is refused for editing; after an edit all UID lines in the file are equal.

quote: The filename should have similar properties as the `UID` of the file content.
test: new_event names the file from the UID: <uid>.ics where uid is restricted to [A-Za-z0-9._@-], no leading dot, no slash.

quote: However, there is no requirement for these two to be the same.
test: File abc.ics containing UID xyz is found by UID xyz and edited in place under the name abc.ics.

quote: ...they *must not* assume that the metadata they included will be preserved by other programs.
test: No behaviour depends on information encoded in the file name beyond the .ics extension; renaming a file does not change which event it represents.

update_event on abc.ics writes the new content to abc.ics (via rename of a temp file onto it); no abc.ics.bak and no rename to <uid>.ics. The first fetch reported this sentence in paraphrase; a second literal fetch did not return it, so it is not marked quoted.

quote: Creating and modifying items or metadata files *should* happen atomically
test: Write goes to <name>.tmp in the same directory (same device), is fsynced, then renamed onto the target; a crash simulated between write and rename leaves the old content intact.

quote: For this purpose, files with the extension `.tmp` may be created inside collections.
test: The temp file name ends in .tmp (not .ics) so a reader scanning *.ics never sees a half-written file.

quote: Any file ending with the `.tmp` or no file extension *must not* be treated as an item.
test: Directory with x.ics, y.ics.tmp and a file named color: only x.ics is loaded as an event; a stale .tmp is neither read nor deleted by the readers.
Event files are written with the .ics extension (vCard uses .vcf); the reader loads *.ics only. First fetch paraphrased the page (iCalendar items use .ics); not copied verbatim.

quote: None of the files listed below have any file extensions.
test: Metadata files (color, displayname, description, order) have no extension and are never parsed as events.

quote: Its content is an ASCII-encoded hex-RGB value of the form `#RRGGBB`.
test: A color file containing #FF8800 is accepted; #f80, red and #FF8800FF are rejected on read and never written.
reason: The server only reads the colour for display if at all; no tool writes the color file.

test: A calendar path is one collection directory; sub-directories are not scanned for events (page text paraphrased by the fetch tool).
Input VCALENDAR with METHOD:REQUEST and one VEVENT: after any edit tool the output has no METHOD line anywhere (backs RFC4791:4.1:no-method; RFC 5546 and 6047 are silent on stored objects).
A file containing METHOD:PUBLISH is listed and expanded normally (METHOD ignored); it is not an error.

Two-attendee event, respond ACCEPTED as me: the diff between input and output is exactly my ATTENDEE PARTSTAT value, DTSTAMP and LAST-MODIFIED; SEQUENCE, ORGANIZER, the other ATTENDEE and every other line are unchanged (confirms the earlier note).

Declining the instance 2026-11-21T10:00Z of weekly series u appends a VEVENT with the same UID, RECURRENCE-ID:20261121T100000Z, its own DTSTAMP, and the ATTENDEE list copied from the master with my PARTSTAT=DECLINED; the master is unchanged except DTSTAMP/LAST-MODIFIED per policy.

Event with ATTENDEE lines but no ORGANIZER: respond_to_event returns an error and the file is not modified (confirms the earlier note: ATTENDEE implies a group-scheduled entity, which needs ORGANIZER).
respond_to_event with our address absent from every ATTENDEE returns an error naming the event, file untouched; the address is compared after stripping a mailto: prefix, case-insensitively.
ATTENDEE;RSVP=TRUE;PARTSTAT=NEEDS-ACTION after respond ACCEPTED: decide whether RSVP=TRUE stays or is removed; either way exactly one RSVP or none.
reason: No RFC requirement; RSVP only asks the organizer's client for a reply, which we do not send. Revisit when a user-visible need appears.

test: Tool descriptions state that only the local calendar file changes and that the organizer is not notified; no mail or network call is made by any tool.
update_event input that names a new organizer returns an error; the existing ORGANIZER line stays byte-identical.
Event with ORGANIZER and no ATTENDEE is read and edited normally, ORGANIZER is kept, no ATTENDEE appears (confirms the earlier note; RFC 5546 3.2.1 PUBLISH has exactly this shape).

We are organizer (ORGANIZER address equals our configured address): DTSTART/DTEND/DURATION/RRULE/RDATE/EXDATE/STATUS change gives SEQUENCE+1 once per edit call (not once per property); a SUMMARY-only change gives no bump.
We are only an attendee and edit SUMMARY or time: SEQUENCE is unchanged and the tool result warns that the organizer will not learn of the change.

Every edit sets DTSTAMP and LAST-MODIFIED on the touched VEVENT(s) to the injected clock in UTC; with a clock earlier than the stored DTSTAMP (skew) the value is max(stored, clock) so it never decreases.

Weekly series ended after 2026-12-05: master RRULE gets UNTIL in the form required by DTSTART's type, COUNT is removed, EXDATE and RECURRENCE-ID overrides after the cutoff are removed so no orphan overrides remain.

Edit one field of a file with X-WR-CALNAME, X-APPLE-* properties, CONFERENCE, IMAGE, VALARM and a CN=a^xb parameter: every line not intentionally changed is byte-identical after unfold/refold normalisation, and a parameter is only re-encoded when its value was edited.

RECURRENCE-ID;TZID=Europe/Berlin:20261121T110000 and RECURRENCE-ID:20261121T100000Z denote the same instance and are matched as one (compare as instants); a DATE instance never matches a DATE-TIME one.

new_event with injected random source writes <uuid>.ics in the configured calendar directory; the path stays inside that directory for any caller input; an existing file of that name is never overwritten.
A file with two UIDs, or a VEVENT plus a VTODO, makes update_event, respond_to_event and end_event_series return an error without writing, rather than guessing which component to change.
A generated VTIMEZONE has TZID plus at least one STANDARD or DAYLIGHT sub-component, each with DTSTART, TZOFFSETFROM and TZOFFSETTO (RFC 5545 3.6.5), and exists exactly once per TZID used.
